title: Computer-Use 2.0: Agents Just Got Multi-Cursor — Francesco Bonacci, Cua
talk_summary: Cua presents Quad Driver, a background computer-use driver that observes a window via accessibility tree/screenshot and executes GUI actions, plus Quad Bench evals and a demand-based sandbox pool for RL training. The transferable parts are eval harness design, reward-hacking checks, scoped observations, release regression harnesses, and warm sandbox pooling; most GUI/RL specifics do not apply.

takeaways.what_they_do: They keep a pool of pre-started sandboxes and autoscale its size from current demand so expensive workers do not wait on sandbox startup/reset.
takeaways.numbers: sandboxes can be 2-4x cheaper than GPUs

takeaways.what_they_do: Each eval task has a setup function, a golden trajectory/oracle, and an evaluator that probes the environment for success, all reproducible via CLI.
takeaways.numbers: 130 verifiable tasks, 42 environments, five platforms; top agent 6/25; no model >30% reward

takeaways.what_they_do: Before accepting an eval task, they run a matrix of agents trying to reward-hack or break the environment; only tasks surviving that pipeline enter the dataset.
takeaways.evidence_quote: We have a matrix of agents attempt to do reward hacking and attempting to break the environment

takeaways.what_they_do: Their computer-use tool focuses on the active window's accessibility tree plus screenshot rather than the entire desktop, reducing irrelevant context.
takeaways.evidence_quote: KU driver focuses on a window rather than the entire desktop

takeaways.what_they_do: They maintain multiple application harnesses to verify new releases do not break behavior across environments.
